sewer-ooze.name: Sewer Ooze
sewer-ooze.blurb: These amorphous masses of sewage and other detritus make their way through filthy culverts beneath cities large and small.

abilities.name: Motion Sense 60 feet
abilities.desc: A sewer ooze can sense nearby motion through vibration and air movement.

abilities.name: Filth Wave
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per minute

Effect The sewer ooze unleashes a wave of filth, covering all creatures in a 20-foot emanation. Each creature in the area must succeed at a DC 17 Reflex save or take 1d4 acid damage and take a –10-foot penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute (on a critical failure, the creature also falls Prone).

A creature can spend an Interact action to clean someone off, decreasing the Speed penalty by 5 feet with each action.

Effect: Filth Wave

tiger-topiary.name: Tiger Topiary
tiger-topiary.blurb: Tiger topiaries are most often found within the Impossible Lands and Tian Xia, adding a dangerous appearance to an enchanting garden. Souls of very proud and volatile individuals can become tiger topiaries, turning into silent stalkers and hunters. Following intruders throughout their territory until they're at their most vulnerable, they're known to pick off unsuspecting adventuring parties one member at a time. Seamlessly blending into nature, only experienced travelers can spot a tiger topiary in time to plot a different course.

abilities.name: Stalker
abilities.desc: When in dense foliage or tall grass, the tiger topiary gains a +1 status bonus to checks to Hide.

abilities.name: Pounce
abilities.desc: The tiger topiary Strides or Leaps and makes a Strike at the end of that movement. If it began this action Hidden, it remains hidden until after this ability's Strike.

abilities.name: Pruning
abilities.desc: The tiger topiary twists and contorts its shape, shedding branches and leaves as needed to change into a topiary of a Medium or smaller animal. Until the next time it acts, the topiary has an automatic result of 32 for Deception checks and DCs to appear as a mundane topiary.

abilities.name: Walk Through Plants
abilities.desc: The tiger topiary ignores difficult terrain caused by dense vegetation.

adept.name: Adept
adept.blurb: Adepts have unlocked only the most minor of occult mysteries. A few are chosen by accomplished practitioners for further training.

abilities.name: Focused Thinker
abilities.desc: The adept concentrates to muster knowledge and wisdom. While focusing, they gain a +2 status bonus to checks to Recall Knowledge, but take a –2 penalty to Perception. They can Dismiss this focused state.

skeletal-mage.name: Skeletal Mage
skeletal-mage.blurb: Rarely, the bones of a spellcaster can be used to create a skeleton that retains a limited ability to cast spells. These spells are almost always offensive in nature, and the skeletal mage uses them with reckless abandon. Skeletal mages are often misidentified as liches, and while not nearly as cunning or deadly, they still pose a significant threat to their foes.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Lasting Debilitating Strike
abilities.desc:
Trigger The xun's Strike hits an Off-Guard creature and deals damage

Effect The xun applies one of the following debilitations, which lasts until the end of the xun's next turn or for 1 week on a critical hit.

Debilitation The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds.

Debilitation The target becomes Enfeebled 1.

Effect: Lasting Debilitating Strike

Effect: Lasting Debilitating Strike (Critical Hit)

abilities.name: Looming Threat
abilities.desc: The master xun Steps or Feints, then Demoralizes.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: The master xun deals an extra 3d6 precision damage to Off-Guard opponents.

zombie-giant-bat.name: Zombie Giant Bat
zombie-giant-bat.blurb: While big bats are certainly not uncommon in dark caves and abandoned ruins and may instill fear in squeamish spelunkers, the so-called giant bat is a true monster, weighing well over 100 pounds and having a wingspan of nearly 15 feet. It primarily eats fruit and bugs, but can be incited to violence through fear or hunger. Giant bat attacks can quickly give rise to rumors of more dangerous monsters—many mistake these massive animals for some sort of demon or vampiric monster. But like other bats, giant bats are simply social and intelligent mammals. They are sometimes used as mounts by smaller humanoids, commonly those who hail from or dwell in mountainous or underground regions.

abilities.name: Slow
abilities.desc: A zombie is permanently Slowed 1 and can't use reactions.

abilities.name: Clumsy Flier
abilities.desc: While a zombie giant bat can fly, its wings are barely able to keep it aloft. If it's airborne when it takes a critical hit or any amount of slashing damage, it falls and it can't Fly on its next turn.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Rotting Aura
abilities.desc: 10 feet. The zombie giant bat emits an aura of rot and disease that cause wounds to fester. Any living creature that starts its turn within the aura and isn't at full Hit Points takes 1d6 void damage.

abilities.name: Clever Gambit
abilities.desc:
Trigger The agent critically hits a creature that they've identified with Recall Knowledge

Effect The agent Steps or Strides. This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the triggering creature.

abilities.name: Consider Options
abilities.desc: The agent Recalls Knowledge about a creature they can see. On a success, the subject is Off-Guard to the agent until the end of the agent's next turn (or for 1 minute on a critical success).

abilities.name: Debilitating Strike
abilities.desc:
Requirements The agent's last action was a successful Strike against an Off-Guard creature

Effect Until the end of the agent's next turn, the target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds or becomes Enfeebled 1. The agent decides which penalty to apply.

Effect: Debilitating Strike

abilities.name: Deny Advantage
abilities.desc: The agent isn't Off-Guard to hidden, undetected, or flanking creatures of their level or lower, or creatures their level or lower using surprise attack.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: The agent deals an additional 3d6 precision damage to creatures that are Off-Guard to them.

abilities.name: Surprise Attack
abilities.desc: If the agent rolled Deception or Stealth for initiative, creatures that haven't yet acted are off-guard to them.

undead-brain-collector.name: Undead Brain Collector
undead-brain-collector.saveNote: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

abilities.name: Absorb Phantom Brain
abilities.desc:
Trigger The undead brain collector possesses at least 1 phantom brain after using Brainlash

Effect The undead brain collector absorbs 1d4 of its phantom brains, gaining 1d8 temporary Hit Points for each brain it absorbed.

abilities.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic
Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Brainlash
abilities.desc:
The undead brain collector extrudes a writhing tangle of ectoplasm from its bursted brain blisters. These ectoplasmic strands lash out at all living targets within 30 feet. Targets in this area must attempt a DC 25 Will save.

After the undead brain collector uses this ability, seven phantom brains glow and shimmer where its brain blisters once were. It can't use Brainlash again until all seven phantom brains are Absorbed.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes 4d6 mental damage.

Failure The creature takes 8d6 mental damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes 8d6 mental damage and is Confused.

abilities.name: Mind-Rotting Toxin
abilities.desc:
Saving Throw basic DC 25 Fortitude save

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 1d6 void and Stupefied 1 (1 round)

Stage 2 1d6 void, stupefied 1, and Slowed 1 (1 round)

Stage 3 2d6 void, Stupefied 2, and slowed 1 (1 round)

clockwork-shambler.name: Clockwork Shambler
clockwork-shambler.blurb: A zombie shambler is a slow-moving horror dangerous in larger groups.

abilities.name: Slow
abilities.desc: A zombie is permanently Slowed 1 and can't use reactions.

abilities.name: Grab
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.

witchs-gaze.name: Witch's Gaze
witchs-gaze.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #4-12: Negotiations for the Star Gun

abilities.name: Bloodletting
abilities.desc: When the witch's gaze deals piercing or slashing damage to an Off-Guard target, they also deal 1 persistent bleed damage.

abyssal-warhound.name: Abyssal Warhound
abyssal-warhound.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #4-99: Blessings of the Forest

abilities.name: Caustic Drool
abilities.desc:
Caustic saliva drips from the warhound's mouth. Until the end of its turn, the abyssal warhound's jaws Strike deals an additional 2 points of acid damage on a successful attack, or 4 points on a critical success.

Effect: Caustic Drool

abilities.name: Shake
abilities.desc:
Requirements The abyssal warhound's Caustic Drool ability is active

Effect The warhound shakes its head, splattering nearby creatures with caustic saliva. All creatures within 10 feet of the warhound take 2d4 acid damage (basic DC 14 Reflex save) and the warhound's Caustic Drool ability ends. Abyssal warhounds are immune to this damage.

accursed-succubus.name: Accursed Succubus
accursed-succubus.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #4-99: Blessings of the Forest
accursed-succubus.blurb: Succubi are manifestations of the sin of destructive lust, and they are the most attractive of all demons-as befits their role in seducing mortals to fall to sin. The concept of gender is fluid to a succubus, as they can adopt countless humanoid forms of any gender to aid in their goals. Most succubi have a feminine true form (incubi, which usually have a masculine true form, are a different kind of demon), but regardless of gender, a lust demon is supernaturally beautiful or handsome, but with curving horns, bat wings, sharp claws, and a sinuous tail.
accursed-succubus.languageNote: three additional mortal languages, telepathy 100 feet, tongues
accursed-succubus.saveNote: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

abilities.name: Telepathy 100 feet
abilities.desc: A monster with telepathy can communicate mentally with any creatures within the listed radius, as long as they share a language. This doesn't give any special access to their thoughts, and communicates no more information than normal speech would.

abilities.name: Constant Spells
abilities.desc: A constant spell affects the monster without the monster needing to cast it, and its duration is unlimited. If a constant spell gets counteracted, the monster can reactivate it by spending the normal spellcasting actions the spell requires.

abilities.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic
Rejection Vulnerability
abilities.desc: As succubi are beings of pure lust, creatures that reject their lust can metaphysically harm them. When a succubus fails a Diplomacy check to Embrace or Request, or when a creature succeeds at its save against a succubus's mental spell or ability, the succubus takes 2d6 mental damage. For one hour after causing mental damage to a succubus in this way, a creature can deal 2d6 mental damage to the succubus with a successful Demoralize incorporating its rejection.

abilities.name: Seductive Presence
abilities.desc: 10 feet. Any creature in the aura that could be sexually attracted to a succubus takes a -2 circumstance penalty to checks and DCs to oppose the succubus's mental spells, Deception, and Diplomacy.

abilities.name: Change Shape
abilities.desc:
The succubus can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

The monster changes its shape indefinitely. It can use this action again to return to its natural shape or adopt a new shape. Unless otherwise noted, a monster cannot use Change Shape to appear as a specific individual. Using Change Shape counts as creating a disguise for the Impersonate use of Deception. The monster's transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine whether the creature is a member of the ancestry or creature type into which it transformed, and it gains a +4 status bonus to its Deception DC to prevent others from seeing through its disguise. Change Shape abilities specify what shapes the monster can adopt. The monster doesn't gain any special abilities of the new shape, only its physical form. For example, in each shape, it replaces its normal Speeds and Strikes, and might potentially change its senses or size. Any changes are listed in its stat block.

abilities.name: Embrace
abilities.desc: The succubus attempts to Grapple a creature using their Diplomacy bonus instead of Athletics. If the creature is willing, the succubus grapples it automatically.

abilities.name: Passionate Kiss
abilities.desc:
Frequency Once per round.

Effect The succubus engages a creature they have Grabbed in an embrace or other act of passion to drain its vital essence. The kiss makes the creature Drained 1 or increases its drained condition by 1, to a maximum of 4. The creature takes 2d6 void damage and the succubus regains Hit Points equal to the damage dealt. The target must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or be affected by a Suggestion to submit to more actions of passion rather than trying to Escape.

abilities.name: Profane Gift
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day.

Effect The succubus on can give a willing humanoid a profane gift. That creature gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws. As long as the gift persists, the succubus can communicate telepathically with the target at any distance, see through the creature's senses, and target the creature with Suggestion through the telepathic link. In addition, the creature uses an outcome one degree of success worse than it rolls on saving throws against the lust demon's suggestion.

A humanoid can't have more than one profane gift at a time, and a succubus can't grant more than one profane gift at a time. Removing the gift requires an Atone ritual. The succubus can remove the gift as a free action to give the recipient a permanent Stupefied 3 condition. A 4th-rank Restoration spell is required to reduce this stupefied condition by 1. A summoned succubus can't grant a profane gift.

Effect: Profane Gift

pathfinder-sentinel.name: Pathfinder Sentinel
pathfinder-sentinel.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #6-00: Salt of the Ocean
pathfinder-sentinel.blurb: When a creature dies, and for whatever reason its spirit is unable or unwilling to leave the site of its death, that spirit may manifest as a poltergeist: a restless, invisible spirit that is still able to manipulate physical objects. Many poltergeists perished in a way that resulted from or led to extreme emotional trauma.

abilities.name: Site Bound
abilities.desc: A Pathfinder sentinel is tied to the wreck of the Whippoorwill and can't travel more than 120 feet from it.

abilities.name: Natural Invisibility
abilities.desc: A poltergeist is naturally Invisible. It becomes visible only when it uses Frighten.

abilities.name: Rejuvenation
abilities.desc: When a poltergeist is destroyed, it reforms, fully healed, where it was destroyed after 2d4 days. A poltergeist can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

abilities.name: Telekinetic Defense
abilities.desc:
Trigger A creature approaches within 10 feet of the poltergeist

Effect The poltergeist makes a telekinetic object Strike against the triggering creature.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Frighten
abilities.desc:
Requirements The poltergeist must be Invisible

Effect The poltergeist becomes visible, appearing as a skeletal, ghostlike humanoid. Each creature within 30 feet must attempt a DC 21 Will save, becoming Frightened 2 on a failure. On a critical failure, it's also Fleeing for as long as it's frightened. On a success, the creature is temporarily immune for 1 minute.

At the start of its next turn, the poltergeist becomes invisible again.

abilities.name: Telekinetic Storm
abilities.desc:
The poltergeist telekinetically throws numerous small objects, such as rocks and pieces of wreckage, either spreading them out among multiple foes or directing them at one target.

  • When this effect is spread out among multiple foes, the poltergeist makes a telekinetic object Strike at a -2 penalty against each creature within 30 feet. These count as one attack for the poltergeist's multiple attack penalty, and the penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks.
  • When this effect has only one target, the poltergeist makes a telekinetic object Strike against the target, and the damage increases to 3d12. It deals 1d12 untyped damage on a failure, and no damage on a critical failure.

zombie-burster.name: Zombie Burster
zombie-burster.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #6-10: Once in Whispers

abilities.name: Bursting Pustules
abilities.desc:
Trigger The zombie takes piercing damage or damage from a critical hit

Effect The pustules covering the zombie's flesh rupture, covering adjacent creatures with vile fluid. Creatures adjacent to the zombie become Sickened 1 unless they succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Grab
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.

experienced-aspis-associate.name: Experienced Aspis Associate
experienced-aspis-associate.src: Pathfinder Society Quest #25: The Greengold Dilemma

abilities.name: Jack of All Actions
abilities.desc: The Associate attempts an Acrobatics, Athletic, Deception, or Intimidation check that uses no more than one action against a creature then makes a strike against the same creature. If the skill action succeeded the strike is made with a +1 circumstance bonus to the attack roll and deals an additional 1d8 precision damage.

abilities.name: Poison Weapon
abilities.desc: The aspis associate applies a contact poison or injury poison to one of their weapons; if they have a free hand, they can Interact to draw a poison as part of this action. They begin combat with a simple injury poison (as from the Poison Weapon rogue feat) already applied to their rapier and one dagger.

noppera-bo-impersonator-martial.name: Noppera-Bo Impersonator (Martial)
noppera-bo-impersonator-martial.src: Pathfinder Season of Ghosts Hardcover Compilation
noppera-bo-impersonator-martial.blurb: Noppera-bos are faceless yokai who delight in tricking others. The noppera-bo impersonators present in this adventure are direct manifestations of Kugaptee's lingering presence in Governor Heh Shan-Bao's mindscape. When this latest mindscape cycle began, the duplicate PCs who dwelled in this mindscape were like the other townsfolk—phantasmal but harmless. As the PCs grew in power in the Willowshore mindscape, the sinister thought energy in Heh Shan-Bao's mindscape reacted and transformed the PCs' duplicates into dangerous monsters: noppera-bo impersonators.

abilities.name: Telepathy 30 feet
abilities.desc: A monster with telepathy can communicate mentally with any creatures within the listed radius, as long as they share a language. This doesn't give any special access to their thoughts, and communicates no more information than normal speech would.

abilities.name: No Face
abilities.desc: The noppera-bo has no sense of vision, but their hearing is precise. They don't breathe and are immune to effects that require breathing. They gain sustenance by absorbing fluids through their skin—traditionally by immersing their hands or faceless head into the fluid to "drink" through osmosis; they can also benefit from consumables, such as potions or elixirs, in this way.

abilities.name: Sensitive Hearing
abilities.desc: As long as the noppera-bo is Deafened, they're Slowed 1.

abilities.name: False Weapon
abilities.desc: A noppera-bo impersonator carries a +1 striking weapon that looks identical to the favored weapon of the character being impersonated. If the PC favors unarmed Strikes, it appears as handwraps. If the impersonated character favors a ranged weapon, then the noppera-bo impersonator has no melee weapon and instead uses the ranged false weapon Strike above; otherwise, the noppera-bo impersonator has no ranged weapon. If the character favors no weapon, then the noppera-bo wields a club as their false weapon. This false weapon is only partially real and inflicts only mental damage when it hits; it gains none of the original weapon's traits or magical enhancements. If a noppera-bo impersonator's false weapon is broken, disarmed, or set down, it fades away. The noppera-bo impersonator can craft a replacement false weapon by spending 10 minutes to recreate one.

abilities.name: Impersonated Abilities
abilities.desc:
The noppera-bo impersonator gains one of the following abilities of your choice.

Effect: Impersonated Ability

  • Armored The noppera-bo appears to be heavily armored, and they increase their AC to 24.
  • Reactive Strike
  • Shield Carrier The noppera-bo carries a Sturdy Shield (Minor) (that transforms into a useless prop if it's destroyed, dropped, or upon the noppera-bo's death), and they gain the Shield Block general feat.
  • Weapon Perk The noppera-bo chooses one of these weapon traits to add to their false weapon: agile, deadly d8, forceful, parry, reach, shove, sweep, or trip.

abilities.name: Devil's Cursed Breath
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day

Effect Jordus bites down on his tongue (taking 1 slashing damage), then exhales a 15-foot cone of burning smoke. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 26 Reflex save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes 3d8 fire damage.

Failure The creature takes 7d8 fire damage and is Sickened 1 by the agonizing pain of the burns.

Critical Failure The creature takes 10d8 fire damage, is sickened 1 by the agonizing pain of the burns, and becomes cursed. The victim's burns never fully vanish, and the cursed creature takes a –2 status penalty to all attacks from the constant pain. Healing doesn't alter the appearance of the burns or lessen the penalty, but removing the curse does.

Effect: Devil's Cursed Breath

abilities.name: Bravado in Numbers
abilities.desc: As long as Thorgrim is adjacent to an ally, he gains a +1 circumstance bonus to all Will saves

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: Thorgrim deals an additional 1d6 precision damage to Off-Guard foes.

abilities.name: You're Next
abilities.desc:
Trigger Thorgrim reduces a foe to 0 Hit Points

Effect Thorgrim attempts to Demoralize a creature within 60 feet, with a +2 circumstance bonus.

radlight-cap.name: Radlight Cap
radlight-cap.blurb: The radlights caps that flourish in many parts of Nar-Voth look like softly glowing, halfling-sized toadstools: a relatively common sight in the Darklands. When radlight caps change color, however, their dangerous nature becomes evident. With each color change, the fungi gain a new set of stimuli that trigger their deadly spore clouds. While a field of blue mushrooms may have attacked noisy interlopers, when they shift to red they assault anyone who moves a muscle. Many Nar-Voth natives, even non-sentient ones, have learned the colors and corresponding behaviors that will see them safely through a field of radlight caps.

abilities.name: Tremorsense (Imprecise) 30 feet
abilities.desc: Tremorsense allows a monster to feel the vibrations through a solid surface caused by movement. It is an imprecise sense with a limited range (listed in the ability). Tremorsense functions only if the monster is on the same surface as the subject, and only if the subject is moving along (or burrowing through) the surface.

abilities.name: Telepathy 100 feet
abilities.desc: A monster with telepathy can communicate mentally with any creatures within the listed radius, as long as they share a language. This doesn't give any special access to their thoughts, and communicates no more information than normal speech would.

abilities.name: Color Change
abilities.desc:
At the start of each round, the radlight cap changes color, going in order from red to yellow to green to blue and back to red, provided the radlight cap is alive and isn't black. Multiple radlight caps encountered within 100 feet of each other synchronize their color changes, such that all caps are the same color at the same time.

At the start of each round, if a radlight cap is within 100 feet of an object or creature that emits radiation, the radlight cap's color changes to black. While black, the radlight cap loses its Radlight aura and can't take actions or reactions.

abilities.name: Lifesense (Imprecise) 30 feet
abilities.desc: Lifesense allows a monster to sense the vital essence of living and undead creatures within the listed range. The sense can distinguish between the vitality energy animating living creatures and the void energy animating undead creatures, much as sight distinguishes colors.

abilities.name: Radlight
abilities.desc: 30 feet. The aura sheds dim light the same color as the radlight cap's current color (see Color Change).

abilities.name: Radlight Spores
abilities.desc:
Trigger The radlight cap takes damage or meets the condition corresponding to its current color, as described below

Effect The radlight cap uses Radlight Spores.

  • Blue The radlight cap detects a sound louder than a whisper.

  • Green A non-fungus creature within 30 feet ends their turn without having moved at least 5 feet.

  • Red A non-fungus creature within 30 feet takes an attack, move, or manipulate action that the radlight cap can detect.

  • Yellow A non-fungus creature within 30 feet ends their turn without being Prone.

abilities.name: Radlight Spores
abilities.desc:
The radlight cap releases a cloud of spores in a 30-foot emanation. The spores deal 2d10 damage (basic DC 24 Fortitude save) to all non-fungus creatures in the area. The type of damage dealt and an additional effect is determined by the radlight cap's current color.

  • Blue The spores deal mental damage. Creatures that fail their save can't breathe or speak for 1 round.

  • Green The spores deal force damage. Creatures that fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from the radlight cap.

  • Red The spores deal fire damage. Creatures that fail their save are Paralyzed for 1 round.

  • Yellow The spores deal electricity damage. Creatures that fail their save are knocked Prone.

djinni.name: Djinni
djinni.blurb: Benevolent genies from the Plane of Air, djinn value art, culture, knowledge, and trade. They also love new experiences, succulent dishes, and heady wines. Of all geniekind, they are most likely to approach humans and other mortals, interacting with them on friendly terms. Still, djinn are proud of their genie heritage and have a tendency to be patronizing toward mortals, a habit that has earned them a reputation for arrogance.

abilities.name: Constant Spells
abilities.desc: A constant spell affects the monster without the monster needing to cast it, and its duration is unlimited. If a constant spell gets counteracted, the monster can reactivate it by spending the normal spellcasting actions the spell requires.

abilities.name: Whirlwind
abilities.desc: 20 feet. All squares in the djinni's aura are difficult terrain for Striding and Flying creatures. Creatures with the air trait are immune.

abilities.name: Hurricane Blast
abilities.desc:
Frequency Once per round.

Effect The djinni all creatures in its whirlwind pushes back 20 feet, or forces all creatures in the aura to move 20 feet clockwise or counterclockwise. Each creature must attempt a DC 21 Fortitude save. On a success, it avoids being moved, and on a critical failure it falls Prone in addition to being moved. Creatures with the air trait are immune.

7.n: Plane Shift (At Will) (to Astral Plane, Elemental Planes, or Material Plane Only)

soulbound-doll-chaotic-evil.name: Soulbound Doll (Chaotic Evil)
soulbound-doll-chaotic-evil.blurb: Soulbound dolls are eerie mannequins or playthings that have been imbued with a small piece of a deceased mortal's soul. These little constructs are created for a variety of reasons-such as to serve as companions or servants-but their free will means their obedience to their creators is hardly a given. Followers of Pharasma generally abhor soulbound dolls, viewing them as a perversion of the natural cycle of souls, and those who worship the Lady of Graves see the destruction of a soulbound doll, regardless of the construct's alignment, as an important service to the Great Beyond. Soulbound dolls are the simplest in a series of soulbound constructs including human-sized soulbound mannequins, powerful soulbound shells, and sentinel soulbound terra-cotta warriors. Creating them from unwilling living creatures is evil, and an unwilling donor can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator's Craft DC, ruining the doll if not preventing the donor's death. A non-evil doll can only be crafted from the soul of a person who has given consent to such use before their death occurred
soulbound-doll-chaotic-evil.languageNote: one spoken by its creator (typically common)

abilities.name: Personality Fragments
abilities.desc: A soulbound doll shares fragments of its donor soul's personality, though none of that creature's memories. This causes a soulbound doll to match the donor soul's alignment and gain the corresponding alignment traits.

soulbound-doll-lawful-evil.name: Soulbound Doll (Lawful Evil)
soulbound-doll-lawful-evil.blurb: Soulbound dolls are eerie mannequins or playthings that have been imbued with a small piece of a deceased mortal's soul. These little constructs are created for a variety of reasons-such as to serve as companions or servants-but their free will means their obedience to their creators is hardly a given. Followers of Pharasma generally abhor soulbound dolls, viewing them as a perversion of the natural cycle of souls, and those who worship the Lady of Graves see the destruction of a soulbound doll, regardless of the construct's alignment, as an important service to the Great Beyond. Soulbound dolls are the simplest in a series of soulbound constructs including human-sized soulbound mannequins, powerful soulbound shells, and sentinel soulbound terra-cotta warriors. Creating them from unwilling living creatures is evil, and an unwilling donor can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator's Craft DC, ruining the doll if not preventing the donor's death. A non-evil doll can only be crafted from the soul of a person who has given consent to such use before their death occurred

abilities.name: Personality Fragments
abilities.desc: A soulbound doll shares fragments of its donor soul's personality, though none of that creature's memories. This causes a soulbound doll to match the donor soul's alignment and gain the corresponding alignment traits.
